claim: CR-007A public-path permissions are a closed set of five literals (report:create, report:read, demand:create, demand:read, demand:withdraw); restricted grants (report:identity-read, artifact access) are explicitly CR-007B, not this package.
quote: /** Public-path permissions ratified by CR-007A. Restricted grants are CR-007B. */

claim: Client-supplied community_ref/subject_id claims on a PublicAuthorizationScope are never treated as authoritative; Ordering must revalidate them against its own membership/grant projections at the boundary.
quote: claims are never authoritative — Ordering revalidates against projections.

claim: Public-path authorization leases have a fixed maximum lifetime of 30,000ms (30s) for interactive protected reads and mutations.
quote: export const PUBLIC_AUTHORIZATION_LEASE_MAX_MS = 30_000;
notes: Cross-referenced SDD §11.1 in the doc comment (version.ts:4).

claim: Membership/grant projection watermarks are considered fresh only within a 60,000ms (60s) ceiling; once exceeded, authorization fails closed regardless of the underlying membership/grant state.
quote: export const PUBLIC_AUTHORIZATION_PROJECTION_MAX_LAG_MS = 60_000;

claim: authorizePublicOperation fails closed with reason unsupported_permission whenever the requested resource+action pair has no entry in REQUIRED_PERMISSION — there is no default-allow for unmapped operations.
quote:
reason: "unsupported_permission",
      safe_code: "forbidden",

claim: authorizePublicOperation runs a fixed independent gate order — permission-match, projection freshness, authoritative scope (tamper), membership, then grant — and any single gate failing aborts the whole check fail-closed with its own reason code.
quote:
assertMembership(input.scope, input.membership);
  assertGrant(input.scope, input.grants);
notes: Confirmed independently revocable by protocol.test.ts 'denies permission revoked while membership remains'.

claim: A caller-supplied community_ref that does not match the server's authoritativeCommunityRef is rejected as reason scope_tamper / safe_code authorization_scope_mismatch — cross-community scope tampering is a distinct fail-closed gate, independent of membership/grant checks.

A caller-supplied subject_id that does not match the server's authoritativeSubjectId is rejected under a distinct reason (cross_subject) from community tampering (scope_tamper), but both map to the identical public safe_code authorization_scope_mismatch — the BFF-facing response never reveals which dimension of the scope was tampered with.

The AuthorizationDenial envelope returned to BFF callers is deliberately narrowed to {schema_version, code, reason} — a closed literal enum on both fields — so no cross-tenant or cross-subject identifying detail is ever surfaced in a denial response.
quote: /** Safe denial envelope returned to BFF callers — no cross-tenant hints. */

claim: The CR-006→public-authorization bridge (resolutionScopeToPublic) accepts only the report:create permission and refuses (as scope_tamper) to synthesize a PublicAuthorizationScope for any resolution scope missing an explicit community_ref — it will not infer or default a community.
HTTP wiring and durable projection ingestion are deliberately kept out of this package; both remain owned by @freeside/ordering-service. This package is contract/decision logic only.
quote: HTTP wiring and durable projection ingestion remain in `@freeside/ordering-service`.

claim: Identity API membership streams and restricted grants (report:identity-read, artifact access) are explicitly excluded from CR-007A's scope and deferred to CR-007B — a deliberate boundary between public-path and restricted authorization.
quote:
Identity API membership
streams and restricted grants (`report:identity-read`, artifact access) are
CR-007B.

claim: Every public-authorization wire schema (scope, watermarks, lease, denial) decodes with errors:"all" and onExcessProperty:"error" — any excess/unknown field on the wire fails the decode, not just a schema_version mismatch.

SigningKeyRegistryDocument requires at least one key, an integer registry_generation >= 1, max_staleness_ms >= 1, a 64-hex distribution_digest, and a schema_version pinned to the single literal SIGNING_KEY_CUSTODY_SCHEMA_VERSION — an empty-keys registry or a fractional/zero staleness bound cannot decode.
quote:
schema_version: Schema.Literal(SIGNING_KEY_CUSTODY_SCHEMA_VERSION),
  registry_id: Schema.String.pipe(Schema.minLength(1), Schema.maxLength(128)),

claim: Fixture signing keys are identified purely mechanically: any signing_key_id containing the literal substring "-fixture-" is classified fixture; any id without it is classified production. There is no separate out-of-band flag for this distinction.
quote: export const FIXTURE_KEY_ID_MARKER = "-fixture-" as const;

claim: A key's custody_backend must match its key_class: fixture keys must use custody_backend "local-fixture"; production keys must use one of aws-kms/gcp-kms/azure-keyvault/vault-transit/cloudhsm. Any other pairing is a key_class_backend_mismatch.
quote:
if (keyClass === "fixture") return custodyBackend === FIXTURE_BACKEND;
  return PRODUCTION_BACKENDS.has(custodyBackend);

claim: validateKeyClassMechanics rejects any key whose declared key_class disagrees with its own signing_key_id naming pattern (invalid_key_id_pattern) — and when the mismatch is a production key wearing a fixture-shaped id, the rejection additionally carries remediation emergency_revoke rather than a soft warning.

satisfiesProductionReleaseGate requires every key in a set to independently pass assertProductionAuthorizedKey (production key_class + production backend + valid id pattern); a fixture-scoped registry can structurally never satisfy a production release gate (G1B-4).
quote: /** Release gates must never treat fixture registry proof as production authorization. */
notes: Cross-referenced by docs/runbook-game-day.md 'Fixture proof must not satisfy this check.'

claim: PinnedKeyRegistry's constructor enforces every key's key_class matches the enclosing document's key_class_scope; a fixture key inside a document declared key_class_scope:"production" (or vice versa) throws ContractIntegrityError at construction time, before any intake request is ever evaluated.
quote:
if (key.key_class !== document.key_class_scope) {
        throw new ContractIntegrityError({

claim: A registry document is judged stale purely from observedAtMs minus its own published_at exceeding its own max_staleness_ms — staleness is registry-local and self-declared, not a fixed global constant.
quote:
const ageMs = observedAtMs - publishedAtMs;
    if (ageMs > document.max_staleness_ms) {

claim: resolveForIntake evaluates a fixed gate order — registry freshness, key existence, key-class authorization for the requested context (production vs fixture), compromise flag, then active/revoked status — and the first failing gate wins; a compromised production key still gets refused for context mismatch before its compromise flag is even inspected if it was requested in the wrong context.

Production and fixture signing material can never satisfy each other's intake context: assertProductionAuthorizedKey rejects any non-production key_class as fixture_key_in_production_context (remediation fail_closed_until_recovery), and assertFixtureKeyOnly symmetrically rejects any non-fixture key_class as production_key_in_fixture_context.

The RemoteSigningBackend/LocalFixtureSigningBackend authorization check mirrors the registry's production/fixture boundary at the signer layer: a production context paired with a local-fixture backend (or non-production keyClass) is rejected as fixture_key_in_production_context before any signing is attempted.

signWithBackend requires a remote (non-fixture) backend's healthCheck() to report ok BEFORE attempting sign(); a failing health check surfaces as SigningBackendError(operation:"health_check") rather than allowing a raw sign call against a possibly-unavailable KMS/HSM.

validateRotationOverlap rejects any RotationEvent whose overlap_ends_at is not strictly after overlap_starts_at as rotation_overlap_invalid, independent of whether the evaluation instant even falls inside that window.

PinnedKeyRegistry.overlappingRotationWindow does not reimplement overlap semantics — it delegates directly to the underlying ServiceKeyRegistry.overlappingRotationWindow imported from @freeside/trust-envelope-protocol, deliberately reusing CR-009's key-activity definition rather than defining a separate CR-013 notion of 'active'.

applyCompromiseToKeys always sets compromise:true AND back-fills revoked_at from the compromise event's detected_at whenever the key had no prior revoked_at — a compromise event can never leave a key merely flagged-but-still-considered-unrevoked.
quote:
compromise: true,
          revoked_at: key.revoked_at ?? event.detected_at,

claim: applyRevocationToKeys sets revoked_at from the event and defaults compromise to false only when it was previously undefined — an existing compromise:true on a key is never silently reset to false by a later revocation event.
quote: revoked_at: event.revoked_at, compromise: key.compromise ?? false }

claim: EmergencyRevocationPlan's quarantine_signed_intake field is typed as the literal true, not boolean — emergency revocation and quarantining signed intake are contractually inseparable; there is no representable plan that revokes a compromised key without also quarantining intake.
quote: readonly quarantine_signed_intake: true;

claim: Database clock-skew evaluation fails closed with insufficient_time_sources whenever fewer than MIN_INDEPENDENT_TIME_SOURCES (2) authoritative sources are supplied, before any offset or uncertainty is even computed.

When authoritative time sources span more than one region, the per-region median unix_ms is computed and intake blocks as time_source_divergence if the max-min spread across regional medians exceeds 500ms (default) — this regional check runs and can block independently of, and prior to, the raw database-vs-source skew comparison.
quote:
regionalDivergenceMs = Math.max(...regionMedians) - Math.min(...regionMedians);
    if (regionalDivergenceMs > maxRegionalDivergenceMs) {

claim: If a lastGoodAt timestamp is provided and its age exceeds 15x maxSkewMs (i.e. 30s at the default 2s threshold), intake blocks as database_clock_unknown even when the instantaneous measured skew would otherwise pass — a prolonged absence of a passing check is treated as equivalent to an unknown clock, not as 'probably still fine.'

The skew comparison against the 2s ceiling is not the raw measured offset alone — effectiveSkew combines the absolute median offset with the maximum reported source uncertainty, so a source with wide uncertainty bounds tightens the practical margin rather than being ignored.
quote: const effectiveSkew = Math.abs(measuredOffsetMs) + offsetUncertaintyMs;

claim: gateSignedIntake evaluates time-health before resolving the registry key — an otherwise-valid, unrevoked signing key is still refused when the database clock is unhealthy, because time-health is checked strictly ahead of key validity in the gate's own call order.
quote:
assertSignedIntakeTimeHealthy(timeHealth);
    registry.resolveForIntake({ signingKeyId, acceptedAtMs, context });
notes: Confirmed by intake-gate.test.ts: 'blocks intake when time-health fails even with a valid key.'

claim: This package deliberately excludes private key material from the repo entirely: production custody is KMS/HSM-backed via RemoteSigningBackend, and LocalFixtureSigningBackend (synchronous, in-process signing) is reserved for fixture key_class only.
quote:
production custody is KMS/HSM-backed via
  `RemoteSigningBackend`; local signing is fixture-only.

claim: A CR-009 TrustEnvelopeHeader binds producer, signing_key_id, contract ref, event_id, stream_id, stream_epoch, sequence, trust_stream flag, issued_at/expires_at, tenant_scope_digest, capability, and body_digest into one struct that is signed as a unit — none of these fields can be altered independently of the signature.

event_id is the idempotency key for every envelope, but contiguous-sequence enforcement (gap detection, ordering) applies ONLY when trust_stream is true — non-trust-stream envelopes get event_id-only deduplication with no ordering semantics at all.
quote:
// Non-trust streams: event_id idempotency only — no contiguous sequence.
  if (!input.envelope.header.trust_stream) {

claim: Epoch reset is fail-closed in both directions: a trust-stream envelope whose stream_epoch is below the consumer's current epoch is rejected as epoch_resume_forbidden (no resuming an old epoch), and one whose epoch is above current is rejected as epoch_baseline_required until a signed StreamEpochBaseline for the new epoch is installed.

Mixed-minor acceptance is explicit and asymmetric: unknown major always fails closed; a consumer accepts any envelope schema_minor <= its own supported minor and rejects anything higher; strict decoders reject unknown/excess fields regardless of minor.
quote:
- Unknown major always fails closed.
 * - Within the same major, a consumer accepts envelope minors <= its supported minor.
 * - Strict decoders reject unknown fields regardless of minor (onExcessProperty: error).

claim: The compatibility commitment 'required-field additions require major bump' is stated only as a doc comment and an inert mixedMinorRules constant (never consulted by any decoder or assertion) — nothing in the package mechanically prevents a future minor-version schema from adding a required field, so the guarantee currently rests entirely on author discipline, not code.
quote:
* - Optional future minors may add only optional fields; required-field additions require major bump.
 */
notes: mixedMinorRules (versioning.ts:37-42) is a frozen data literal returned for observability only; no call site branches on it to enforce the rule.

claim: TrustEnvelopeRejectedError's reason enum declares unknown_schema_major and schema_minor_unsupported as possible rejection reasons, but the actual schema-version guards (assertSupportedSchemaMajor / assertSupportedSchemaMinor, called from verifyTrustEnvelope) throw a plain Error, never a TrustEnvelopeRejectedError — no code path in the frozen package can produce a TrustEnvelopeRejectedError carrying either of these two declared reasons, so a consumer pattern-matching on that error's .reason field will never observe them.
quote:
readonly reason:
    | "unknown_schema_major"
    | "schema_minor_unsupported"
notes: Cross-checked: versioning.ts:20-35 throws new Error(...) at both sites; verify.ts:26-27 is the only call site and does not catch/rewrap into TrustEnvelopeRejectedError. grep across all non-test trust-envelope src files confirms zero throw sites for these two reason strings as TrustEnvelopeRejectedError.

claim: verifyTrustEnvelope runs a fixed gate order — schema major/minor, body-digest match, key existence, key active/revoked, producer binding, capability binding, tenant-scope binding, issued-in-future, expiry, then Ed25519 signature — each an independent fail-closed check with its own reason code, signature verification happening last.

A producer's clock is allowed to lead the consumer's accepted-at time by at most 30,000ms (30s) before an envelope is rejected as issued_in_future; the doc comment cites SDD §11.1 as the source of this specific ceiling.
quote:
/** Producer clock may lead consumer authority by at most 30 seconds (SDD §11.1). */
export const TRUST_ENVELOPE_MAX_FUTURE_SKEW_MS = 30_000;

claim: Minimum trust-stream retention is 86,400,000ms (24h), justified as covering live resolution/order reconciliation per SDD §11.1; the consumer rejects further ingestion as retention_violation (remediation request_replay_range) once the oldest retained acceptedAt falls outside that window.
quote:
/** Minimum stream retention covering live resolution/order reconciliation (SDD §11.1). */
export const TRUST_STREAM_MIN_RETENTION_MS = 86_400_000;

claim: Trust-stream sequence acceptance is strictly contiguous, one envelope at a time: on sequence_gap the consumer records the missing range for repair but must NOT commit the envelope's event_id and must NOT advance highestContiguousSequence. This corrects the package's own initial v1.0.0 release logic (commit 0804dfb1), which committed event_id/retainedAcceptedAtMs unconditionally before the sequence checks ran and auto-advanced highestContiguousSequence across previously-recorded gaps via a while-loop — meaning a gapped envelope's event_id was poisoned and its own later, correctly-ordered redelivery could be silently skipped. package.json still declares version 1.0.0 with no version bump across this behavior-changing fix (commit 0791a090).
notes: Pre-fix code (removed by 0791a090) read: 'state.highestContiguousSequence = sequence; state.gaps.delete(sequence); while (state.gaps.has(state.highestContiguousSequence + 1)) { state.highestContiguousSequence += 1; state.gaps.delete(state.highestContiguousSequence); }' with event_id/retainedAcceptedAtMs committed unconditionally earlier in the function, per `git show 0791a090`. package.json version field confirmed literally "1.0.0" at af064179.

claim: The fix for the sequence-gap defect states its own rationale directly in the commit message: BB review on PR #497 found the consumer could skip gaps or poison event_id on sequence_gap; the corrected contract is that trust-stream envelopes accept in contiguous order only, and a sequence_gap rejection must record the missing sequences WITHOUT committing event_id, specifically so redelivery after gap repair remains possible.

The test suite makes the BB #497 fix a machine-checked invariant: after a sequence_gap rejection, the envelope's event_id must be absent from seenEventIds and highestContiguousSequence must be unchanged; redelivering the identical jumped-ahead envelope again still yields sequence_gap (never event_id_replay) until the missing range is actually repaired in order.
quote:
// BB #497: gap reject must not poison event_id or skip missing sequences.
      expect(gapResult.state.seenEventIds.has(gap!.envelope.header.event_id)).toBe(false);

claim: replayEnvelopeIdempotently only short-circuits as a true idempotent replay (accepted, replay:true, no re-verification) when the prior envelope's event_id exactly equals the incoming envelope's event_id AND that event_id is already present in seenEventIds; a mismatched prior/incoming event_id is rejected outright as event_id_replay rather than falling through to full re-ingestion.

Installing a new stream-epoch baseline requires the baseline's stream_epoch to be strictly greater than the consumer's previous epoch (epoch_not_advanced otherwise), its baseline_digest to exactly equal an independently-computed expectedBaselineDigest (baseline_incomplete otherwise), and a valid Ed25519 signature from a known, active signing key — only after all three pass does the consumer reset its gap set and adopt the baseline's highest_sequence as the new floor.

A ServiceSigningKey is 'active' only if compromise is not true, activated_at is at or before the evaluation instant, and (when present) revoked_at is strictly after the evaluation instant. The compromise check is evaluated first and short-circuits regardless of the key's activation/revocation timing.

overlappingRotationWindow requires the previous and next keys to share the same producer, both be independently 'active' at the evaluation instant, and have different signing_key_ids — a rotation can never be valid across two different producers, and a rotation into an already-revoked or compromised key never counts as a valid overlap.

Signing bytes for both TrustEnvelope and StreamEpochBaseline are computed over the JCS-canonicalized structure with the signature field forced to an empty-string placeholder, then SHA-256 hex-digested and UTF-8 encoded as the message actually signed — canonicalization happens strictly before hashing, and the signature never covers itself.

This package's CR-009 trust envelope is explicitly declared distinct from the events-pillar acvp-l1-v2 NATS envelope, despite superficially similar 'signed envelope' shape — the two are not meant to be conflated or treated as interchangeable.
quote:
CR-009 signed trust-envelope wire contract for collection-report Ordering
dependency intake. Distinct from the events-pillar `acvp-l1-v2` NATS envelope.

claim: Production signing-key custody is explicitly out of scope for this package and remains owned by CR-013 (signing-key-custody); this package publishes wire semantics and non-production fixture keys only.
quote:
Production signing-key custody remains CR-013. This package publishes wire
semantics and non-production fixture keys only.

claim: jcsCanonicalize fails closed (throws) rather than silently coercing whenever its input is not JSON-representable (functions, symbols, Infinity, NaN, BigInt without toJSON, or undefined at root) — canonicalization never lossy-serializes an unrepresentable value.
